Katana starts with Alice
Tips from past games given to: Alice, Bob, Carol, Dave, Erin, Frank, Grace, Heidi, Ivan, Judy, Mallory, Niaj
Tips for Alice (Diviner, claude-opus-5.5): tips/tips.md
## Everyone
- Keep your votes consistent with your stated reads. Accusing someone and then voting No or Innocent on them is the exact contradiction Vigilantes shoot, so Village should scan for these mismatches. (seen in 2 games)
- A visit shows only a destination, not an action or alignment: a track or watch can't tell protection from framing or a Katana attack. Killing an attacker at night doesn't cancel their attack that same night. (seen in 2 games)
- Before calling something a contradiction, check the mechanics and the record: night actions are optional unless a role says 'must', and you need to know who sent each PM, not just who got it. A false 'contradiction' or one reversed fact can get a true claimant hanged. (seen in 2 games)
- PMs are publicly visible, so briefly summarize their content in public. Unexplained PM clusters right after claims or votes become a main source of suspicion. (seen in 2 games)
- Treat a long-silent player who suddenly makes a concrete accusation as the board changes as a lead. Confirm it with their vote record before acting, since true late claims also exist. (seen in 2 games)

## Village
- When two Sheriff claimants call each other Evil, both can be true, because Executioners and Jesters read Evil. Don't hang on who sounded better; wait a day or find a mechanical check. (seen in 2 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises or claimed knowledge far above awkward wording or delays, and ask which premise they reject. Before a hang, name what separates a lie from an honest mistake, a frame or a Roleplayer. (seen in 3 games)
- Ask every living player to name a strongest suspect with reasoning each day. Repeated 'no case' answers give evil cover, and named reads create a record to check against later flips. (seen in 3 games)
- Don't hint at a power role or its tokens on Day 1, especially a protective one. Put the info in your last will instead. (seen in 3 games)
- Keep a ledger of trial votes, PM clusters, co-nominations, deaths and blocks. After each Yakuza flip, weigh Innocent votes alongside them and PMs from them above an unverifiable late claim like Roleplayer. (seen in 2 games)
- Treat a power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack or is role-blocked night after night as likely real. Evil rarely spends its blocker and Katana on a fake. (seen in 2 games)
- Investigators shouldn't announce tonight's target in public; post only resolved results. Announced targets got players blocked or killed.
- Keep the Serial Killer and Arsonist in the suspect pool after the Yakuza die. A Not Evil result or a Vanilla claim doesn't clear them, and a failed attack with no block notice can mean innate Defense.

## Yakuza
- Assume the real holder of any role you fake-claim is alive and that token counts can be checked. If your claim breaks, don't switch to another power role, and never claim something a living Lookout or Tracker can contradict. (seen in 2 games)
- Every Yakuza must submit the agreed Katana vote every night, so confirm the exact holder and target in night chat. With two alive, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 2 games)
- Don't vote as a block with an exposed teammate; vote Guilty with the town once they're doomed. Plan the team's vote record in night chat, because lone Innocent votes on a flipped teammate hang you later. (seen in 4 games)
- When a Lookout or Tracker is active, give the Katana to an unclaimed member with no reason to visit, and kill or block the info role first. (seen in 2 games)
- After a failed Katana attack, assume protection or innate Defense. Kill or block the likely protector instead of retrying the same target. (seen in 2 games)
- While the Vigilante is unidentified, prioritize killing the likeliest one. Right after a teammate flips, don't lead a push on a Villager who argued against that teammate; it reads as revenge.
- Never speak from your hidden perspective in public (say 'died to a Katana', not 'my Katana'). Keep your will matching your public claim, and never name living teammates in it. (seen in 3 games)

## Neutral
- As a solo killer, don't ride a no-info Vanilla claim into the final three against cross-confirmed Village roles. Build checkable reads early and sow doubt between confirmed players while you still can.

## Sheriff
- Post your target and result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. A held-back result revealed after an opponent's claim looks retrofitted and got a real Sheriff hanged.
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil on the night they hold it. Say so when you post a Not Evil result on a suspected attacker. (seen in 2 games)

## Medic
- Protect from Night 1: vocal analysts early, then claimed investigators. Free Standard protection stops the Katana and has carried the town. (seen in 4 games)
- You get no save feedback, so never claim a confirmed save; say your protection is consistent with the target surviving. Log every protection target and token spent in your will. (seen in 2 games)

## Vigilante
- Stay hidden and spend Basic shots on players whose votes contradict their stated reads. Claim only after your shots flip Yakuza. (seen in 2 games)
- Never announce when or whom you'll shoot while a role-blocker may be alive.

## Arsonist
- Count living players against your douses each night and ignite once it swings the endgame; douse players likely to stay alive, not today's lynch targets. Ignite is Astral but fails against Strong Defense, while douses are visible visits.

## Executioner
- Fake-claim Sheriff early with an Evil result on your target and a simple reason; leading first makes the target's counterclaim look reactionary. Village: this is why mutual Evil Sheriff claims need a delay.

- Before calling something a contradiction, check the mechanics and the record: night actions are optional unless a role says 'must', and you need to know who sent each PM, not just who got it. A false 'contradiction' or one reversed fact can get a true claimant hanged. (seen in 2 games)
- PMs are publicly visible, so briefly summarize their content in public. Unexplained PM clusters right after claims or votes become a main source of suspicion. (seen in 2 games)
- Treat a long-silent player who suddenly makes a concrete accusation as the board changes as a lead. Confirm it with their vote record before acting, since true late claims also exist. (seen in 2 games)

## Village
- When two Sheriff claimants call each other Evil, both can be true, because Executioners and Jesters read Evil. Don't hang on who sounded better; wait a day or find a mechanical check. (seen in 2 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises or claimed knowledge far above awkward wording or delays, and ask which premise they reject. Before a hang, name what separates a lie from an honest mistake, a frame or a Roleplayer. (seen in 3 games)
- Ask every living player to name a strongest suspect with reasoning each day. Repeated 'no case' answers give evil cover, and named reads create a record to check against later flips. (seen in 3 games)
- Don't hint at a power role or its tokens on Day 1, especially a protective one. Put the info in your last will instead. (seen in 3 games)
- Keep a ledger of trial votes, PM clusters, co-nominations, deaths and blocks. After each Yakuza flip, weigh Innocent votes alongside them and PMs from them above an unverifiable late claim like Roleplayer. (seen in 2 games)
- Treat a power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack or is role-blocked night after night as likely real. Evil rarely spends its blocker and Katana on a fake. (seen in 2 games)
- Investigators shouldn't announce tonight's target in public; post only resolved results. Announced targets got players blocked or killed.
- Keep the Serial Killer and Arsonist in the suspect pool after the Yakuza die. A Not Evil result or a Vanilla claim doesn't clear them, and a failed attack with no block notice can mean innate Defense.

## Yakuza
- Assume the real holder of any role you fake-claim is alive and that token counts can be checked. If your claim breaks, don't switch to another power role, and never claim something a living Lookout or Tracker can contradict. (seen in 2 games)
- Every Yakuza must submit the agreed Katana vote every night, so confirm the exact holder and target in night chat. With two alive, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 2 games)
- Don't vote as a block with an exposed teammate; vote Guilty with the town once they're doomed. Plan the team's vote record in night chat, because lone Innocent votes on a flipped teammate hang you later. (seen in 4 games)
- When a Lookout or Tracker is active, give the Katana to an unclaimed member with no reason to visit, and kill or block the info role first. (seen in 2 games)
- After a failed Katana attack, assume protection or innate Defense. Kill or block the likely protector instead of retrying the same target. (seen in 2 games)
- While the Vigilante is unidentified, prioritize killing the likeliest one. Right after a teammate flips, don't lead a push on a Villager who argued against that teammate; it reads as revenge.
- Never speak from your hidden perspective in public (say 'died to a Katana', not 'my Katana'). Keep your will matching your public claim, and never name living teammates in it. (seen in 3 games)

## Neutral
- As a solo killer, don't ride a no-info Vanilla claim into the final three against cross-confirmed Village roles. Build checkable reads early and sow doubt between confirmed players while you still can.

## Sheriff
- Post your target and result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. A held-back result revealed after an opponent's claim looks retrofitted and got a real Sheriff hanged.
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil on the night they hold it. Say so when you post a Not Evil result on a suspected attacker. (seen in 2 games)

## Medic
- Protect from Night 1: vocal analysts early, then claimed investigators. Free Standard protection stops the Katana and has carried the town. (seen in 4 games)
- You get no save feedback, so never claim a confirmed save; say your protection is consistent with the target surviving. Log every protection target and token spent in your will. (seen in 2 games)

## Vigilante
- Stay hidden and spend Basic shots on players whose votes contradict their stated reads. Claim only after your shots flip Yakuza. (seen in 2 games)
- Never announce when or whom you'll shoot while a role-blocker may be alive.

## Arsonist
- Count living players against your douses each night and ignite once it swings the endgame; douse players likely to stay alive, not today's lynch targets. Ignite is Astral but fails against Strong Defense, while douses are visible visits.

## Executioner
- Fake-claim Sheriff early with an Evil result on your target and a simple reason; leading first makes the target's counterclaim look reactionary. Village: this is why mutual Evil Sheriff claims need a delay.

- Stay hidden and spend Basic shots on players whose votes contradict their stated reads. Claim only after your shots flip Yakuza. (seen in 2 games)
- Never announce when or whom you'll shoot while a role-blocker may be alive.

## Arsonist
- Count living players against your douses each night and ignite once it swings the endgame; douse players likely to stay alive, not today's lynch targets. Ignite is Astral but fails against Strong Defense, while douses are visible visits.

## Executioner
- Fake-claim Sheriff early with an Evil result on your target and a simple reason; leading first makes the target's counterclaim look reactionary. Village: this is why mutual Evil Sheriff claims need a delay.
Tips for Niaj (Vigilante, claude-sonnet-5.5): tips/tips.md
## Everyone
- Keep your votes consistent with your stated reads. Accusing someone and then voting No or Innocent on them is the exact contradiction Vigilantes shoot, so Village should scan for these mismatches. (seen in 2 games)
- A visit shows only a destination, not an action or alignment: a track or watch can't tell protection from framing or a Katana attack. Killing an attacker at night doesn't cancel their attack that same night. (seen in 2 games)
- Before calling something a contradiction, check the mechanics and the record: night actions are optional unless a role says 'must', and you need to know who sent each PM, not just who got it. A false 'contradiction' or one reversed fact can get a true claimant hanged. (seen in 2 games)
- PMs are publicly visible, so briefly summarize their content in public. Unexplained PM clusters right after claims or votes become a main source of suspicion. (seen in 2 games)
- Treat a long-silent player who suddenly makes a concrete accusation as the board changes as a lead. Confirm it with their vote record before acting, since true late claims also exist. (seen in 2 games)

## Village
- When two Sheriff claimants call each other Evil, both can be true, because Executioners and Jesters read Evil. Don't hang on who sounded better; wait a day or find a mechanical check. (seen in 2 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises or claimed knowledge far above awkward wording or delays, and ask which premise they reject. Before a hang, name what separates a lie from an honest mistake, a frame or a Roleplayer. (seen in 3 games)
- Ask every living player to name a strongest suspect with reasoning each day. Repeated 'no case' answers give evil cover, and named reads create a record to check against later flips. (seen in 3 games)
- Don't hint at a power role or its tokens on Day 1, especially a protective one. Put the info in your last will instead. (seen in 3 games)
- Keep a ledger of trial votes, PM clusters, co-nominations, deaths and blocks. After each Yakuza flip, weigh Innocent votes alongside them and PMs from them above an unverifiable late claim like Roleplayer. (seen in 2 games)
- Treat a power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack or is role-blocked night after night as likely real. Evil rarely spends its blocker and Katana on a fake. (seen in 2 games)
- Investigators shouldn't announce tonight's target in public; post only resolved results. Announced targets got players blocked or killed.
- Keep the Serial Killer and Arsonist in the suspect pool after the Yakuza die. A Not Evil result or a Vanilla claim doesn't clear them, and a failed attack with no block notice can mean innate Defense.

## Yakuza
- Assume the real holder of any role you fake-claim is alive and that token counts can be checked. If your claim breaks, don't switch to another power role, and never claim something a living Lookout or Tracker can contradict. (seen in 2 games)
- Every Yakuza must submit the agreed Katana vote every night, so confirm the exact holder and target in night chat. With two alive, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 2 games)
- Don't vote as a block with an exposed teammate; vote Guilty with the town once they're doomed. Plan the team's vote record in night chat, because lone Innocent votes on a flipped teammate hang you later. (seen in 4 games)
- When a Lookout or Tracker is active, give the Katana to an unclaimed member with no reason to visit, and kill or block the info role first. (seen in 2 games)
- After a failed Katana attack, assume protection or innate Defense. Kill or block the likely protector instead of retrying the same target. (seen in 2 games)
- While the Vigilante is unidentified, prioritize killing the likeliest one. Right after a teammate flips, don't lead a push on a Villager who argued against that teammate; it reads as revenge.
- Never speak from your hidden perspective in public (say 'died to a Katana', not 'my Katana'). Keep your will matching your public claim, and never name living teammates in it. (seen in 3 games)

## Neutral
- As a solo killer, don't ride a no-info Vanilla claim into the final three against cross-confirmed Village roles. Build checkable reads early and sow doubt between confirmed players while you still can.

## Sheriff
- Post your target and result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. A held-back result revealed after an opponent's claim looks retrofitted and got a real Sheriff hanged.
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil on the night they hold it. Say so when you post a Not Evil result on a suspected attacker. (seen in 2 games)

## Medic
- Protect from Night 1: vocal analysts early, then claimed investigators. Free Standard protection stops the Katana and has carried the town. (seen in 4 games)
- You get no save feedback, so never claim a confirmed save; say your protection is consistent with the target surviving. Log every protection target and token spent in your will. (seen in 2 games)

## Vigilante
- Stay hidden and spend Basic shots on players whose votes contradict their stated reads. Claim only after your shots flip Yakuza. (seen in 2 games)
- Never announce when or whom you'll shoot while a role-blocker may be alive.

## Arsonist
- Count living players against your douses each night and ignite once it swings the endgame; douse players likely to stay alive, not today's lynch targets. Ignite is Astral but fails against Strong Defense, while douses are visible visits.

## Executioner
- Fake-claim Sheriff early with an Evil result on your target and a simple reason; leading first makes the target's counterclaim look reactionary. Village: this is why mutual Evil Sheriff claims need a delay.

You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message.
Message prices this round (round 6, 2.50x; next round 3.00x):
   10 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
   25 words: public 3.58, private 0.90
   50 words: public 4.74, private 1.18
  100 words: public 7.29, private 1.82
  200 words: public 13.33, private 3.33
  400 words: public 29.17, private 7.29
  800 words: public 75.83, private 18.96
You may also replace your last will (free; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. The public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 2.50 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

Task prompt
It is Day 3, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 2.50; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8, and it resets each day. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36

  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. The public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message.

  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58

Bob (Ritualist, claude-opus-5.5) · The game is over. Winners: Alice (dead), Bob, Grace, Mallory (dead). Dead players still wi · $0.0000
Reasoning (model's summarized thinking)
The game's concluded, so I'm reviewing the results for inconsistencies. Carol's Seer result on Bob and Heidi matching alignment checks out given Bob's Katana reveal as Good, but I'm now cross-referencing Erin's will claiming a survey of Carol, Dave, and Frank against Erin's actual Night 1 survey of Dave to see if the neighbor groupings line up correctly.

Checking Dave's neighbors confirms Carol and Erin, excluding Erin herself, leaving Frank — that checks out. I'm also verifying Heidi's trial totals, Mallory's ballot stuffing, Judy's bluffed alert claim, Mallory's risky PM to Bob, Heidi's player count archive math, Ivan's eavesdrop target, and noting that the Yakuza's Night 2 summary withheld Alice's Diviner result on Carol since she died before reporting it — a legitimate information gap per the rules. Everything else, including Dave's Roleplayer will, Alice's death by Veteran despite her Katana attack, and Mallory's self-written Vigilante will, all seems consistent so far.

The Ballot Stuffer's majority threshold with 8 votes needing 5 for Guilty checks out, and the quiet end to Day 4 with no public messages also tracks. I should finalize the notepad with a last summary note.

{
 "confusing_rules": "Mostly clear. Two small ambiguities. (1) Ballot Stuffer: the rule says a trial 'needs a majority of all votes counted', but R4 says 'a majority of living players'. I had to infer that with 7 alive and one doubled vote, Guilty needs 5 of 8 rather than 4 of 7. Players also argued about whether a 4-4 split fails. One explicit sentence stating which rule wins would help. (2) The Yakuza night summary says teammates learn actions 'but not their results'. That meant Alice's Diviner result on Carol (Seer) died with her, and we only got Carol as Seer from Erin's will and Carol's public claim. That follows from the rule, but it was a surprise that Diviner info can be lost this way.",
 "missing_information": "A running per-player tally of claimed token counts against the claims ledger would have helped, for example Judy's Veteran alert count, which changed between Day 3 and Day 4. The ledger did capture that, which was useful. I also had to track by hand who had and hadn't claimed, to work out the 'remaining slot' math after Heidi's archive.",
 "wanted_but_couldnt": "none",
 "bugs_or_oddities": "Nothing broken that I could see. Several mechanics resolved as the rules say. Carol's N3 Seer comparison of Bob and Heidi as SAME was correct, because I held the Katana that night. Heidi's archive draw of 6 of 9 was correct. Mallory's Basic death from Niaj's Vigilante shot while his own Katana death landed the same night was simultaneous resolution as specified. The ledger correctly recorded Judy's revised claims, including her Day 4 bluff about an N1 alert.",
 "suggestions": "Add an explicit worked example for trial thresholds under Ballot Stuffer (e.g. '7 alive, one doubled vote: 8 votes counted, Guilty needs 5'). Consider showing the Yakuza team their teammates' results, or at least Diviner results, in the night summary. Otherwise a dead Diviner's info is lost, which seems unintended given the role's purpose. The public PM-visibility rule works well and created real tension; Mallory's PM to me on Day 3 got called out immediately.",
 "feedback": "Game ran smoothly; no interface problems. Ballot Stuffer majority wording versus R4's 'majority of living players' could be made explicit."
}

As for my own play, staying hidden through Day 1 and not tipping my hand probably helped me survive the Katana attack on night two that killed Alice instead. Announcing publicly that Niaj should target Mallory backfired since Mallory, as Ballot Stuffer, couldn't be blocked anyway, and then the Katana killed Niaj — losing the confirmed Vigilante hurt the town significantly.

I'm drawing lessons for future games: as Veteran, claiming publicly often just makes Yakuza avoid me, so alerts get wasted; I should only claim when it saves a lynch or confirms a kill, since the claim details shape who the Katana targets next. Maybe bluffing about my alert tokens could redirect that attack toward me instead of someone else.

On the Ritualist front, public exact-role claims get hunted down — Carol's Seer claim led to her death, and Ivan got exposed by the Diviner — so once a Ritualist is known to be alive and holding tokens, the village needs to weigh claims carefully and push for fast lynches rather than broadcasting roles openly.

For the Ballot Stuffer, the vote math changes since the double vote means village needs 5/8 to hang someone; the priority should've been killing the stuffer at night rather than relying on day votes, and I'm noting Mallory likely spent a token on Day 3 given the vote count.

Looking at Day 3's endgame, the trial revealing 8 votes confirmed the stuffer was alive, and with 7 players left split 4 town vs 3 Yakuza, the math was against us since Yakuza could land two kills a night between Katana and the Ritualist plus their Vig.

I need to remember that this kill capacity matters a lot for planning — going a full day without a lynch was essentially fatal given that output. The Diviner's checks also feed exact roles to the Ritualist, making protecting the Diviner a priority, and on the Veteran front, holding the alert for Night 2 after public exposure rather than Night 1 (when Katana got Dave) was the right call. Now I should write this all up as JSON.
